title: Rain Washes Out Final T20I as Australia Women Beat New Zealand 2-0
excerpt: Only 2.4 overs were possible at North Sydney Oval before persistent rain abandoned the third T20I, confirming Australia as 2-0 series winners and Rose Bowl holders.
body:
• The third T20I between Australia and New Zealand women at North Sydney Oval was abandoned after 2.4 overs, with New Zealand 11 for 2.
  • Australia win the three-match series 2-0 and retain the Rose Bowl, having won the opener by two wickets and the second match by 40 runs.
  • Ashleigh Gardner was named player of the series, with 107 runs and two wickets across the two completed matches.
  • The teams meet again in an ODI series in March.

The third and final women's T20I between Australia and New Zealand was washed out at North Sydney Oval on Thursday after only 2.4 overs, confirming Australia as 2-0 series winners in an anti-climactic finish to a competitive series.

Fourteen Overs Became None

Play started more than an hour late, with the match reduced to 14 overs per side. Australia captain Sophie Molineux chose to bowl. New Zealand, who had struggled batting first in game two, reshuffled their order: captain Melie Kerr moved up to open, Izzy Sharp shifted to number three and Flora Devonshire dropped to six.

Kerr hit Molineux's first delivery through the covers for four, then skied the next ball to mid-on — Molineux's 20th wicket in the first over of an innings in her career, according to ESPNcricinfo. Kim Garth then removed Georgia Plimmer with a quicker delivery after a run of slower balls. New Zealand were 11 for 2 when heavy rain returned and did not relent.

How the Series Was Won

Australia had already secured the Rose Bowl before Thursday. In the opener at the same venue, New Zealand made 162 for 2 and Australia chased it down at 165 for 8 with two wickets to spare, Ellyse Perry hitting 52 off 30 balls after a mid-innings collapse. In the second match, Gardner scored 84 off 45 as Australia posted 167 for 7, then took two wickets while Georgia Wareham claimed three, as New Zealand fell 40 runs short at 127 for 8.

Gardner finished as player of the series. All three fixtures were played at North Sydney Oval, and the series was the first T20 cricket either side had played since the T20 World Cup.

An Experiment That Never Got Tested

Both teams named unchanged line-ups for the finale, but New Zealand's reshuffle was the tactical story of the day. After making only 127 for 8 in the second match, the White Ferns promoted their captain to open and moved their biggest hitter up the order — a recognition that their batting, not their bowling, had lost them the series. The rain allowed the new order exactly 16 balls. Kerr's dismissal was also a small piece of history for Molineux: ESPNcricinfo noted it was the 20th time in her career she had taken a wicket in the first over of an innings.

The series doubled as both teams' return to the format after the T20 World Cup, which made the lost finale more than a dead rubber for New Zealand: it was their last chance to test combinations in match conditions before the March ODI series. Australia, by contrast, leave with their first-choice side settled and Gardner in career-best all-round form.

What Comes Next

The rivalry resumes in March, when the teams meet again for an ODI series. For New Zealand, the batting-order experiment begun on Thursday — Kerr opening, Sharp at three — got less than three overs of testing, and remains an open question for that series.
